```{r setup, include=FALSE}
invisible(Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE','English_United States.utf8'))

suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(ggplot2);library(dplyr);library(tidyr)})
root<-normalizePath('../..',winslash='/')
input<-file.path(root,'data','2026_IRD_experiment','processed_data')
pre_dir<-'preliminary_quality_checks';ige_dir<-'ige_estimations'
dir.create(pre_dir,showWarnings=FALSE);dir.create(ige_dir,showWarnings=FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,cache=FALSE,size="small",
 fig.width=10,fig.height=7,dpi=300,out.width='100%',fig.align='center')
set.seed(2026)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=11)+theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
 strip.background=element_rect(fill='#EAF0F4'),legend.position='bottom'))
rd<-function(f)read.csv2(file.path(input,f),fileEncoding='UTF-8-BOM',na.strings='NA')
write_excel<-function(d,f){
 lines<-character();con<-textConnection('lines','w',local=TRUE)
 write.csv2(d,con,row.names=FALSE,na='NA');close(con)
 con<-file(f,'wb');on.exit(close(con));writeBin(as.raw(c(239,187,191)),con)
 writeBin(charToRaw(enc2utf8(paste0(paste(lines,collapse='\r\n'),'\r\n'))),con)
}
stars<-function(p)ifelse(is.na(p),'NA',ifelse(p<.001,'***',
 ifelse(p<.01,'**',ifelse(p<.05,'*','ns'))))
pfmt<-function(p)format.pval(p,digits=3,eps=.001)
avg<-function(x)if(all(is.na(x)))NA_real_ else mean(x,na.rm=TRUE)
grain<-rd('traits_pesee_grains.csv');straw<-rd('traits_pesee_pailles.csv')
metro<-rd('traits_grain_metrologie.csv')
sources<-list(grain=grain,straw=straw,metro=metro)
source_traits<-list(grain=c('poids_grains_g','nb_epis'),straw='poids_pailles_g',
 metro=c('mass_totale_mesuree_g','nb_grains','PMG'))
traits6<-unlist(source_traits,use.names=FALSE)
traits<-setdiff(traits6,'mass_totale_mesuree_g')
labels<-c(poids_grains_g='Grain weight (g)',nb_epis='Number of ears',
 poids_pailles_g='Straw weight (g)',mass_totale_mesuree_g='Instrument mass (g)',
 nb_grains='Number of grains',PMG='Thousand-grain weight (g)')
long<-bind_rows(lapply(names(sources),function(s){
 sources[[s]] %>% mutate(source=s) %>%
 pivot_longer(all_of(source_traits[[s]]),names_to='trait',values_to='value')
})) %>% mutate(trait=factor(trait,levels=traits6))
facets<-function()facet_wrap(~trait,scales='free',ncol=3,labeller=as_labeller(labels))
pot_means<-long %>% group_by(source,trait,pot_id,pot_type,chapelle,row,column) %>%
 summarise(n_observed=sum(!is.na(value)),mean_value=avg(value),
 resown=max(resown),.groups='drop') %>% rename(value=mean_value)
```

# Scope and decisions

All recorded observations are retained, including zeros, resown plants and
harvest comments. Missing responses are not imputed. `resown=1` means that `r`
was recorded in the reseeding column; its original `1` denotes later germination,
not reseeding. Individual mono plants cannot be matched across source files:
their comments/resown flags apply at pot--genotype level.

Preliminary design and pot-type tests use mono/mixt pot means, avoiding treating
two plants sharing a pot as independent. IGE models use individual responses
and fit within-pot correlation. Instrument mass is omitted from IGE models.
Step 3 predictions remain restricted to traits selecting M3.

# Preliminary quality checks

## Distributions and zero counts

```{r distributions, fig.path='preliminary_quality_checks/figures/'}
distribution<-long %>% group_by(trait) %>% summarise(n=sum(!is.na(value)),
 zeros=sum(value==0,na.rm=TRUE),missing=sum(is.na(value)),.groups='drop') %>%
 mutate(annotation=paste0('Zeros: ',zeros,'; n = ',n))
ggplot(filter(long,!is.na(value)),aes(value))+
 geom_histogram(bins=25,fill='#327FA5',colour='white')+facets()+
 geom_label(data=distribution,aes(x=Inf,y=Inf,label=annotation),
 inherit.aes=FALSE,hjust=1.04,vjust=1.1,size=3,linewidth=0)+
 labs(x='Trait value',y='Number of measurements')
knitr::kable(select(distribution,trait,n,zeros,missing),row.names=FALSE)
```

There are `r nrow(grain)` manual grain/straw observations and `r nrow(metro)`
metrology observations. Zero counts are absolute counts, not missing values.
The metrology shortfall is absent rows rather than NA values in existing rows.
Extreme values are retained. Residual distributions, not raw distributions
alone, are relevant to the Gaussian model assumptions.

## Design effects

The following comparisons are marginal Kruskal--Wallis tests. Means based on
one available plant receive the same weight as means based on two. A resown
pot means at least one genotype is recorded as resown. These limitations are
addressed more directly in the subsequent plant-level mixed models.

```{r design, fig.path='preliminary_quality_checks/figures/', fig.height=13, out.height='85%'}
design_factors<-c('chapelle','row','column','resown')
design_data<-bind_rows(lapply(design_factors,function(f){
 pot_means %>% filter(pot_type!='solo',is.finite(value)) %>%
 mutate(factor=f,group=as.character(.data[[f]]))
}))
design_tests<-design_data %>% group_by(trait,factor) %>%
 summarise(n_pots=n(),p=if(n_distinct(group)>1 && n_distinct(value)>1)
 kruskal.test(value~as.factor(group))$p.value else NA_real_,.groups='drop') %>%
 mutate(q=p.adjust(p,'BH'),annotation=paste0(stars(q),' q=',pfmt(q)))
design_data$group<-factor(design_data$group,
 levels=as.character(sort(unique(as.numeric(design_data$group)))))
ggplot(design_data,aes(group,value))+geom_boxplot(fill='#9DC6D8',outlier.shape=NA)+
 geom_point(position=position_jitter(width=.15,seed=2026),alpha=.25,size=.6)+
 facet_grid(trait~factor,scales='free',labeller=labeller(trait=labels))+
 geom_label(data=design_tests,aes(x=Inf,y=Inf,label=annotation),
 inherit.aes=FALSE,hjust=1.02,vjust=1.05,size=2.3,linewidth=0)+
 scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(.04,.2)))+
 labs(x='Factor level',y='Pot mean')+
 theme(axis.text.x=element_text(size=6),strip.text=element_text(size=8))
knitr::kable(design_tests %>% select(trait,factor,n_pots,p,q),digits=4)
```

There are `r sum(design_tests$q<.05,na.rm=TRUE)` associations with BH q < 0.05
across the 24 tests. These are unadjusted for genotype and other design terms,
not causal effects. Ordinal row/column positions include offset end pots and
are not measured physical distances.

## Mono versus mixt

```{r pot-type, fig.path='preliminary_quality_checks/figures/'}

type_tests<-type_data %>% group_by(trait) %>% summarise(
 p=wilcox.test(value~pot_type,exact=FALSE)$p.value,.groups='drop') %>%
 mutate(q=p.adjust(p,'BH'),annotation=paste0(stars(q),' q=',pfmt(q)))
ggplot(type_data,aes(pot_type,value))+geom_boxplot(fill='#9DC6D8',outlier.shape=NA)+
 geom_point(position=position_jitter(width=.12,seed=2026),alpha=.3,size=.8)+facets()+
 geom_label(data=type_tests,aes(x=Inf,y=Inf,label=annotation),

knitr::kable(type_tests %>% select(trait,p,q),digits=4)
```

`r sum(type_tests$q<.05)` traits differ at BH q < 0.05. This marginal comparison
differs from the genetically adjusted pot-type fixed-effect test in step 2.

## Grain-weight method comparison

Only solo/mixt plants can be matched unambiguously across source files.

```{r method-comparison, fig.path='preliminary_quality_checks/figures/'}
keys<-c('pot_id','pot_type','genotype_id','neighbour_id')
a<-grain %>% filter(pot_type!='mono') %>% select(all_of(keys),poids_grains_g)
b<-metro %>% filter(pot_type!='mono') %>% select(all_of(keys),mass_totale_mesuree_g)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(a[keys]),!anyDuplicated(b[keys]))
method_pairs<-inner_join(a,b,by=keys) %>%
 filter(is.finite(poids_grains_g),is.finite(mass_totale_mesuree_g))
method_cor<-cor.test(method_pairs$poids_grains_g,
 method_pairs$mass_totale_mesuree_g,method='pearson')
ggplot(method_pairs,aes(poids_grains_g,mass_totale_mesuree_g))+
 geom_abline(slope=1,intercept=0,linetype=2,colour='grey50')+
 geom_point(aes(colour=pot_type),alpha=.6)+coord_equal()+
 labs(x='Manual grain weight (g)',y='Instrument grain mass (g)',
 subtitle=sprintf('Pearson R = %.5f; nominal p %s; n = %d',
 method_cor$estimate,pfmt(method_cor$p.value),nrow(method_pairs)))
```

Pearson R = `r round(unname(method_cor$estimate),5)` for
`r nrow(method_pairs)` plants. Correlation is association, not agreement; inspect
the equality line too. Nominal inference ignores within-pot dependence.
The near duplication motivates omitting instrument mass from genetic models.

## Pairwise trait correlations

Pot means include all pot types without guessing mono plant matches. Spearman
correlations are used consistently because several traits are discrete/skewed.

```{r trait-correlations, fig.path='preliminary_quality_checks/figures/', fig.height=8}
wide<-pot_means %>% select(pot_id,trait,value) %>%
 pivot_wider(names_from=trait,values_from=value)
cor_pairs<-bind_rows(lapply(combn(traits6,2,simplify=FALSE),function(pair){
 xy<-wide[,pair];xy<-xy[complete.cases(xy),]
 z<-cor.test(xy[[1]],xy[[2]],method='spearman',exact=FALSE)
 data.frame(first=pair[1],second=pair[2],n=nrow(xy),rho=unname(z$estimate),p=z$p.value)
})) %>% mutate(q=p.adjust(p,'BH'),stars=stars(q))
tiles<-bind_rows(cor_pairs,cor_pairs %>% rename(first=second,second=first),
 data.frame(first=traits6,second=traits6,n=nrow(wide),rho=1,p=NA,q=NA,stars='')) %>%
 mutate(x=factor(first,levels=traits6),y=factor(second,levels=rev(traits6)),
 text=paste0(sprintf('%.2f',rho),ifelse(stars=='ns','',stars)))
ggplot(tiles,aes(x,y,fill=rho))+geom_tile(colour='white')+
 geom_text(aes(label=text),size=3)+coord_fixed()+
 scale_fill_gradient2(low='#C84A4A',mid='white',high='#287BB5',limits=c(-1,1))+
 scale_x_discrete(labels=labels)+scale_y_discrete(labels=labels)+
 theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=35,hjust=1))+
 labs(x=NULL,y=NULL,fill='Spearman',subtitle='Pot means; BH stars across 15 pairs')
```

`r sum(cor_pairs$q<.05)` pairs have BH q < 0.05. Associations pool genotype,
spatial and pot-type effects. Incomplete pots use available measurements.
They do not identify genetic correlations or causal relationships.

# IGE estimation

## Equations and terms

For focal genotype $i$ with neighbour $j$, the shared fixed part is
\[
F=\mu+\mathrm{Chapelle}_c+\beta_r\mathbf1(\mathrm{resown})
  +\beta_m\mathbf1(\mathrm{mono}).
\]
The final term is omitted when the pot-type testing rule below drops it.
\[
\begin{aligned}
M1:\ y_{ip}&=F+R_{c,r}+C_{c,k}+D_i+e_{ip},\\
M2:\ y_{ip}&=F+R_{c,r}+C_{c,k}+D_i+I_j+e_{ip},\\
M3:\ y_{ip}&=F+R_{c,r}+C_{c,k}+D_i+I_j+S_{ij}+e_{ip}.
\end{aligned}
\]
$R_{c,r}$ and $C_{c,k}$ are random row and column effects within chapelle;
$D_i$ is focal DGE, $I_j$ neighbour IGE and $S_{ij}$ the directed pair effect,
distinct from $S_{ji}$. These have normal distributions with their own variances.
In M2/M3 the same genotype's DGE and IGE have covariance
\[
(D_g,I_g)'\sim N\left(0,
\begin{bmatrix}\sigma_D^2&\sigma_{DI}\\\sigma_{DI}&\sigma_I^2\end{bmatrix}\right),
\quad\sigma_{DI}=\rho_{DI}\sigma_D\sigma_I.
\]
Different genotypes are independent: no additive relationship matrix is used.
Two residuals sharing a pot have covariance
\[
R_p=\sigma_e^2\begin{bmatrix}1&\rho_e\\\rho_e&1\end{bmatrix};
\]
different pots are independent. Row/column and pair effects are independent
of each other and of the DGE/IGE block. Count traits also use Gaussian models.

```{r model-data}
trait_file<-c(poids_grains_g='traits_pesee_grains.csv',nb_epis='traits_pesee_grains.csv',
 poids_pailles_g='traits_pesee_pailles.csv',nb_grains='traits_grain_metrologie.csv',
 PMG='traits_grain_metrologie.csv')
prepare<-function(t){
 d<-rd(trait_file[[t]]);d<-d[d$pot_type!='solo',];d$response<-d[[t]]
 d<-do.call(rbind,lapply(split(d,d$pot_id),function(z){
  miss<-setdiff(1:2,z$plant_id)
  if(length(miss)){
   stopifnot(nrow(z)==1,length(miss)==1)
   extra<-z;extra$plant_id<-miss;extra$response<-NA_real_
   extra$genotype_id<-z$neighbour_id;extra$neighbour_id<-z$genotype_id
   ref<-grain[grain$pot_id==extra$pot_id & grain$genotype_id==extra$genotype_id,]
   extra$resown<-ref$resown[1];z<-rbind(z,extra)
  };z
 }))
 d<-d[order(d$pot_id,d$plant_id),];rownames(d)<-NULL
 g<-sort(unique(c(d$genotype_id,d$neighbour_id)))
 d$DGE<-factor(d$genotype_id,levels=g);d$IGE<-factor(d$neighbour_id,levels=g)
 d$DGExIGE<-factor(paste0('g',d$genotype_id,'_n',d$neighbour_id))
 d$chapelle<-factor(d$chapelle);d$resown<-factor(d$resown)
 d$pot_type<-factor(d$pot_type,levels=c('mixt','mono'))
 d$row_group<-interaction(d$chapelle,d$row,drop=TRUE)
 d$column_group<-interaction(d$chapelle,d$column,drop=TRUE)
 d$pot<-factor(d$pot_id);d$plant<-factor(d$plant_id,levels=1:2)
 stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(d[c('pot','plant')]),all(table(d$pot)==2));d
}
data_list<-setNames(lapply(traits,prepare),traits)
```

NA response slots complete the residual grid; they do not impute phenotypes.

## Pot-type fixed-effect tests and fitting

A conditional asymptotic Wald test ($z^2$, one degree of freedom) tests the
mono coefficient in each M1/M2/M3 fit. This does not compare REML likelihoods
with different fixed structures. Raw p < 0.05 screens pot type. A trait retains
it in all three candidates if any candidate supports it; otherwise all three
drop it. Thus each subsequent REML LRT has identical fixed terms. Screening,
model selection and variance-parameter uncertainty are not propagated into
nominal Wald/LRT p-values.

```{r fitting-functions}
random_forms<-list(M1=~row_group+column_group+DGE,
 M2=~row_group+column_group+str(~DGE+IGE,~corgh(2):id(DGE)),
 M3=~row_group+column_group+str(~DGE+IGE,~corgh(2):id(DGE))+DGExIGE)
fit_model<-function(d,m,with_type){
 fixed<-if(with_type)response~chapelle+resown+pot_type else response~chapelle+resown
 once<-function(gp=list(),rp=list())asreml::asreml(fixed=fixed,
  random=random_forms[[m]],residual=~id(pot):corv(plant),data=d,
  G.param=gp,R.param=rp,na.action=asreml::na.method(y='include',x='fail'),
  maxit=100,workspace='256mb',trace=FALSE)
 f<-once();if(!isTRUE(f$converge))f<-update(f,maxit=100)
 if(!isTRUE(f$converge))stop('Nonconverged model: ',m)
 if(m!='M1'){
  base<-f
  for(rho in c(-.8,0,.8)){
   gp<-base$G.param
   for(term in names(gp))for(j in seq_along(gp[[term]])){
    b<-gp[[term]][[j]];if(!is.null(b$con))b$con[b$con=='B']<-'P'
    gp[[term]][[j]]<-b
   }
   gp[['DGE+IGE']][['2']]$initial[]<-
    c(rho,.15*var(d$response,na.rm=TRUE),.05*var(d$response,na.rm=TRUE))
   gp[['DGE+IGE']][['2']]$con<-c('U','P','P')
   candidate<-try(once(gp,base$R.param),silent=TRUE)
   valid<-!inherits(candidate,'try-error') && isTRUE(candidate$converge)
   if(valid && candidate$loglik>f$loglik)f<-candidate
  }
 };f
}
```

```{r pot-type-tests}
full_models<-list();pot_tests<-list();keep_type<-setNames(logical(length(traits)),traits)
for(t in traits){
 full_models[[t]]<-setNames(lapply(names(random_forms),function(m)
  fit_model(data_list[[t]],m,TRUE)),names(random_forms))
 pot_tests[[t]]<-bind_rows(lapply(names(random_forms),function(m){
  co<-summary(full_models[[t]][[m]],coef=TRUE)$coef.fixed
  ix<-match('pot_type_mono',rownames(co));stopifnot(!is.na(ix))
  estimate<-co[ix,'solution'];se<-co[ix,'std error']
  data.frame(trait=t,model=m,mono_minus_mixt=estimate,SE=se,
   p=pchisq((estimate/se)^2,1,lower.tail=FALSE))
 }))
 keep_type[t]<-any(pot_tests[[t]]$p<.05)
}
pot_tests<-bind_rows(pot_tests)
knitr::kable(pot_tests,digits=4,row.names=FALSE)
```

Pot type retained for: **`r if(any(keep_type))paste(names(keep_type)[keep_type],collapse=', ')else 'none of the traits'`**.
Dropping it does not prove its effect is zero; the allocation of average
mono--mixt differences among genetic terms changes.

## Model selection

M1--M2 jointly tests IGE variance and DGE--IGE covariance, using the asymptotic
mixture $0.5\chi^2_1+0.5\chi^2_2$. M2--M3 tests one interaction variance using
$0.5\chi^2_0+0.5\chi^2_1$. With ten genotypes and boundary estimates these
approximations warrant caution. Select M3 if M3--M2 has p < 0.05; otherwise
select M2 if M2--M1 has p < 0.05, else M1. BH across ten tests is supplementary.

```{r selection}
models<-list();lrt<-list();selection<-list()
for(t in traits){
 models[[t]]<-if(keep_type[t])full_models[[t]] else
  setNames(lapply(names(random_forms),function(m)fit_model(data_list[[t]],m,FALSE)),
   names(random_forms))
 compare<-function(a,b,joint){
  delta<-b$loglik-a$loglik
  if(delta< -1e-3)stop('Nested likelihood ordering failed: ',t)
  LR<-max(0,2*delta)
  p<-if(LR==0)1 else if(joint)
   .5*pchisq(LR,1,lower.tail=FALSE)+.5*pchisq(LR,2,lower.tail=FALSE) else
   .5*pchisq(LR,1,lower.tail=FALSE)
  data.frame(LR=LR,p=p)
 }
 a<-compare(models[[t]]$M1,models[[t]]$M2,TRUE)
 b<-compare(models[[t]]$M2,models[[t]]$M3,FALSE)
 best<-if(b$p<.05)'M3' else if(a$p<.05)'M2' else 'M1'
 selection[[t]]<-data.frame(trait=t,pot_type_retained=keep_type[t],selected=best)
 lrt[[t]]<-rbind(cbind(data.frame(trait=t,comparison='M1 to M2'),a),
  cbind(data.frame(trait=t,comparison='M2 to M3'),b))
}
selection<-bind_rows(selection);lrt<-bind_rows(lrt) %>% mutate(q=p.adjust(p,'BH'))
knitr::kable(selection,row.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(lrt,digits=5,row.names=FALSE)
```

Selected models: `r paste(paste(selection$trait,selection$selected),collapse='; ')`.
There are `r sum(lrt$p<.05)` nominally significant and `r sum(lrt$q<.05)`
BH-significant tests. These data do not warrant treating interaction selection
as robust without sensitivity or bootstrap checks.

## Marginal phenotypic variance shares

The average conditional individual-plant variance, over the observed mono/mixt
composition, is
\[
V_P=\sigma_D^2+\sigma_I^2+\sigma_S^2+2p_{mono}\sigma_{DI}
 +\sigma_R^2+\sigma_C^2+\sigma_e^2.
\]
$p_{mono}$ is the fraction of observed plant responses in mono pots. In mixt
pots different genotype effects are independent; in mono pots the same
genotype supplies DGE and IGE, adding $2\sigma_{DI}$. Each component's share is
$100v_k/V_P$. The covariance share is $100(2p_{mono}\sigma_{DI})/V_P$ and can
be negative. Signed shares sum to 100%. Within-pot residual correlation changes
between-plant covariance, not individual variance, and is not an additional
variance component. Shares condition on fixed effects: they are not fractions
of raw sample variance, total breeding-value variance, or causal contributions.

```{r variance-functions}
getv<-function(vc,n)as.numeric(vc[n,'component'])
genetic_block<-function(f,m){
 vc<-summary(f)$varcomp
 if(m=='M1')return(c(D=getv(vc,'DGE'),I=0,cov=0,rho=NA))
 vd<-getv(vc,'DGE+IGE!corgh(2)_1');vi<-getv(vc,'DGE+IGE!corgh(2)_2')
 ix<-startsWith(rownames(vc),'DGE+IGE!') & endsWith(rownames(vc),'.cor')
 rho<-as.numeric(vc[ix,'component']);stopifnot(length(rho)==1)
 c(D=vd,I=vi,cov=rho*sqrt(vd*vi),rho=rho)
}
variance<-bind_rows(lapply(traits,function(t){
 m<-selection$selected[selection$trait==t];f<-models[[t]][[m]]
 vc<-summary(f)$varcomp;g<-genetic_block(f,m);d<-data_list[[t]]
 pm<-mean(d$genotype_id[!is.na(d$response)]==d$neighbour_id[!is.na(d$response)])
 v<-c(DGE=g[['D']],IGE=g[['I']],Interaction=if(m=='M3')getv(vc,'DGExIGE')else 0,
  Covariance=2*pm*g[['cov']],Row=getv(vc,'row_group'),
  Column=getv(vc,'column_group'),Residual=as.numeric(vc[endsWith(rownames(vc),'!var'),'component']))
 data.frame(trait=t,component=names(v),variance=as.numeric(v),percent=100*v/sum(v))
}))
```

```{r variance-plot, fig.path='ige_estimations/figures/'}
variance$component<-factor(variance$component,
 levels=c('DGE','IGE','Interaction','Covariance','Row','Column','Residual'))
ggplot(variance,aes(trait,percent,fill=component))+geom_col(width=.7)+
 scale_fill_manual(values=c('#277DA8','#E69F00','#8A62AA','#B95442',
 '#B9C7C9','#D4DDDE','#EEEEEE'))+
 labs(x=NULL,y='Share of modelled individual-plant variance (%)',fill='Component')+
 theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=25,hjust=1))
knitr::kable(variance %>% filter(component %in% c('DGE','IGE','Interaction','Covariance')) %>%
 select(trait,component,percent),digits=3,row.names=FALSE)
```

## Genetic predictions and joint model-based errors

Only M3-selected traits are exported. The DGE baseline is $B_i=\mu+D_i$.
The directed interaction contribution is
$H_{ij}=I_j+S_{ij}+\beta_m\mathbf1(i=j)$ when pot type is retained, and
$I_j+S_{ij}$ when it is dropped. The interaction file has a single combined
interaction column. Adding the baseline and interaction gives the fitted
reference-condition one-neighbour expectation (chapelle 1, non-resown, zero
random row/column effects). The baseline is not solo yield: it comes from the
competition model with neighbour effects set to their population means.

Joint errors must retain covariances between fixed and genetic terms and
between different predictions. For $\theta=(\beta',u')'$, the error variance
of $a'\widehat\theta$ is $a'C_\theta a$, not the sum of component SEs.
With $V=ZGZ'+R$, define
\[
 C_\beta=(X'V^{-1}X)^{-1},\quad K=GZ'V^{-1},\quad B=KX.
\]
The joint BLUE/BLUP error covariance is
\[
C_\theta=\begin{bmatrix}
 C_\beta&-C_\beta B'\\
 -BC_\beta&G-KZG+BC_\beta B'
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
We reconstruct this matrix from ASReml variance estimates and the observed-data
design, then check coefficients and their standard errors against ASReml.
For the joint prediction vector, with contrast matrix $L$,
\[
C_{pred}=LC_\theta L'.
\]
The prediction tables report $\sqrt{\mathrm{diag}(C_{pred})}$ and approximate
95% bounds (estimate $\pm1.96$ SE). The complete joint covariance is exported
per trait, with matching `prediction_id` labels. A grid prediction with weights
$w$ has model-based error variance $w'C_{pred}w$, including reuse of the same
effect across several neighbours.

These errors condition on estimated variance parameters and the selected
model. They exclude variance-parameter/model-selection uncertainty and the
uncertainty of transferring one-neighbour effects to a grid. Bounds describe
latent expectations, not intervals for a new plant's phenotype; future residual
variation is not added. The mono fixed contrast, if retained, is experimental
pot-type adjustment, not a calibrated response to multiple same-genotype
neighbours.

```{r joint-errors}
joint_errors<-function(f,d,m,with_type){
 d<-d[!is.na(d$response),]
 fixed<-if(with_type)~chapelle+resown+pot_type else ~chapelle+resown
 X<-model.matrix(fixed,d);stopifnot(qr(X)$rank==ncol(X))
 xnames<-colnames(X)
 for(term in c('chapelle','resown','pot_type'))
  xnames<-sub(paste0('^',term),paste0(term,'_'),xnames)
 colnames(X)<-xnames
 zfactor<-function(v,term){
  z<-model.matrix(~v-1);colnames(z)<-paste0(term,'_',levels(v));z
 }
 Zparts<-list(zfactor(d$row_group,'row_group'),
  zfactor(d$column_group,'column_group'),zfactor(d$DGE,'DGE'))
 vc<-summary(f)$varcomp;g<-genetic_block(f,m)
 ng<-nlevels(d$DGE);nr<-nlevels(d$row_group);nc<-nlevels(d$column_group)
 if(m!='M1')Zparts<-c(Zparts,list(zfactor(d$IGE,'IGE')))
 if(m=='M3')Zparts<-c(Zparts,list(zfactor(d$DGExIGE,'DGExIGE')))
 Z<-do.call(cbind,Zparts);G<-matrix(0,ncol(Z),ncol(Z))
 diag(G)<-c(rep(getv(vc,'row_group'),nr),rep(getv(vc,'column_group'),nc),
  rep(g[['D']],ng),if(m!='M1')rep(g[['I']],ng),
  if(m=='M3')rep(getv(vc,'DGExIGE'),nlevels(d$DGExIGE)))
 if(m!='M1'){
  di<-nr+nc+seq_len(ng);ii<-nr+nc+ng+seq_len(ng)
  G[cbind(di,ii)]<-g[['cov']];G[cbind(ii,di)]<-g[['cov']]
 }
 rho<-as.numeric(vc[endsWith(rownames(vc),'!plant!cor'),'component'])
 ve<-as.numeric(vc[endsWith(rownames(vc),'!var'),'component'])
 R<-ve*((1-rho)*diag(nrow(d))+rho*outer(d$pot_id,d$pot_id,'=='))
 V<-Z%*%G%*%t(Z)+R;Vi<-chol2inv(chol(V))
 Cb<-solve(crossprod(X,Vi%*%X));K<-G%*%t(Z)%*%Vi;B<-K%*%X
 beta<-as.numeric(Cb%*%crossprod(X,Vi%*%d$response))
 u<-as.numeric(K%*%(d$response-X%*%beta))
 Cu<-G-K%*%Z%*%G+B%*%Cb%*%t(B)
 C<-rbind(cbind(Cb,-Cb%*%t(B)),cbind(-B%*%Cb,Cu));C<-(C+t(C))/2
 cn<-c(colnames(X),colnames(Z));dimnames(C)<-list(cn,cn)
 theta<-setNames(c(beta,u),cn)
 cf<-summary(f,coef=TRUE)$coef.fixed;cr<-summary(f,coef=TRUE)$coef.random
 ref<-c(cf[match(colnames(X),rownames(cf)),'solution'],
  cr[match(colnames(Z),rownames(cr)),'solution'])
 ref_se<-c(cf[match(colnames(X),rownames(cf)),'std error'],
  cr[match(colnames(Z),rownames(cr)),grep('^std[ .]error$',colnames(cr),value=TRUE)[1]])
 difference<-max(abs(theta-ref),na.rm=TRUE)
 se_difference<-max(abs(sqrt(pmax(0,diag(C)))-ref_se),na.rm=TRUE)
 stopifnot(difference<.005,se_difference<.005)
 list(theta=theta,C=C,estimate_check=difference,SE_check=se_difference)
}
prediction_dge<-prediction_interaction<-error_checks<-list()
for(t in selection$trait[selection$selected=='M3']){
 d<-data_list[[t]];f<-models[[t]]$M3;with_type<-keep_type[t]
 j<-joint_errors(f,d,'M3',with_type);g<-levels(d$DGE)
 pairs<-expand.grid(genotype=g,neighbour=g,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
 id_d<-paste0('DGE:',t,':',g)
 id_h<-paste0('interaction:',t,':',pairs$genotype,':',pairs$neighbour)
 L<-matrix(0,length(g)+nrow(pairs),length(j$theta),
  dimnames=list(c(id_d,id_h),names(j$theta)))
 for(i in seq_along(g))L[i,c('(Intercept)',paste0('DGE_',g[i]))]<-1
 for(i in seq_len(nrow(pairs))){
  ix<-length(g)+i
  L[ix,c(paste0('IGE_',pairs$neighbour[i]),
   paste0('DGExIGE_g',pairs$genotype[i],'_n',pairs$neighbour[i]))]<-1
  if(with_type && pairs$genotype[i]==pairs$neighbour[i])L[ix,'pot_type_mono']<-1
 }
 values<-as.numeric(L%*%j$theta);CP<-L%*%j$C%*%t(L)
 stopifnot(min(eigen(CP,symmetric=TRUE,only.values=TRUE)$values)> -1e-6)
 se<-sqrt(pmax(0,diag(CP)));nd<-length(g);ih<-nd+seq_len(nrow(pairs))
 prediction_dge[[t]]<-data.frame(trait=t,genotype=g,prediction_id=id_d,
  intercept=j$theta[['(Intercept)']],DGE_BLUP=j$theta[paste0('DGE_',g)],
  prediction=values[seq_len(nd)],prediction_formula='intercept + DGE',
  prediction_SE=se[seq_len(nd)],
  lower95=values[seq_len(nd)]-1.96*se[seq_len(nd)],
  upper95=values[seq_len(nd)]+1.96*se[seq_len(nd)],
  reference_chapelle=levels(d$chapelle)[1],reference_resown=levels(d$resown)[1],
  reference_pot_type=if(with_type)'mixt' else 'not fitted',row.names=NULL)
 prediction_interaction[[t]]<-data.frame(trait=t,pairs,prediction_id=id_h,
  interaction=values[ih],
  prediction_formula=ifelse(with_type & pairs$genotype==pairs$neighbour,
    'IGE + DGE:IGE + mono fixed effect','IGE + DGE:IGE'),
  prediction_SE=se[ih],
  lower95=values[ih]-1.96*se[ih],upper95=values[ih]+1.96*se[ih],
  pot_type_adjustment_included=with_type & pairs$genotype==pairs$neighbour)
 write_excel(data.frame(prediction_id=rownames(CP),CP,check.names=FALSE),
  file.path(ige_dir,paste0('prediction_error_covariance_',t,'.csv')))
 error_checks[[t]]<-data.frame(trait=t,max_estimate_difference=j$estimate_check,
  max_SE_difference=j$SE_check)
}
DGE<-if(length(prediction_dge))bind_rows(prediction_dge)else
 data.frame(trait=character(),genotype=character(),prediction=numeric(),prediction_SE=numeric())
interactions<-if(length(prediction_interaction))bind_rows(prediction_interaction)else
 data.frame(trait=character(),genotype=character(),neighbour=character(),
 interaction=numeric(),prediction_SE=numeric())
write_excel(DGE,file.path(ige_dir,'03_DGE_genotype_predictions.csv'))
write_excel(interactions,file.path(ige_dir,'03_all_genotype_interactions.csv'))
knitr::kable(bind_rows(error_checks),digits=7,row.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(DGE %>% select(trait,genotype,prediction,prediction_SE),digits=4,row.names=FALSE)
```

The two main prediction files contain `r nrow(DGE)` baselines and
`r nrow(interactions)` directed interactions. The covariance file supplies the
error covariance for their concatenated vector. Baselines have the intercept
added; interactions do not. Same-genotype and different-genotype predictions
are together, and only same-genotype predictions include a mono contrast if
that fixed term was retained. No individual genotype CSVs are generated.

### Solo BLUEs versus competition DGE predictions

The `prediction_formula` column states which fitted terms enter each exported
prediction. The baseline is `intercept + DGE`; interaction predictions contain
neighbour IGE plus the directed pair effect, with a mono fixed adjustment only
if that term was retained. Prediction SEs use the joint errors for exactly
those terms.

For comparison with solo performance, genotype is fitted as a **fixed effect**
in a separate ASReml model using all available solo observations:
\[
y_{ip}=\mu_s+\mathrm{Chapelle}_c+\beta_{r,s}\mathbf1(\mathrm{resown})
       +G_i+R_{c,r}+C_{c,k}+e_{ip}.
\]
The solo expectation is the intercept plus genotype BLUE. Chapelle and resown
are fixed, row/column within chapelle are random, and residuals are independent.
Pot type cannot be fitted within a solo-only dataset and no within-pot residual
correlation is estimable. Both comparisons refer to chapelle 1 and non-resown
plants, with random spatial effects set to zero.

```{r solo-blue-comparison, fig.path='ige_estimations/figures/'}
# Solo BLUEs use fixed genotype and all applicable design corrections.
# Pot type is constant for solo plants; no residual pair exists within a pot.
solo_comparisons<-solo_correlations<-list()
for(t in unique(DGE$trait)){
 solo<-rd(trait_file[[t]])
 solo<-solo[solo$pot_type=='solo' & is.finite(solo[[t]]),]
 solo$response<-solo[[t]]
 solo$genotype<-factor(solo$genotype_id,
   levels=sort(unique(solo$genotype_id)))
 solo$chapelle<-factor(solo$chapelle)
 solo$resown<-factor(solo$resown)
 solo$row_group<-interaction(solo$chapelle,solo$row,drop=TRUE)
 solo$column_group<-interaction(solo$chapelle,solo$column,drop=TRUE)
 solo_fit<-asreml::asreml(fixed=response~chapelle+resown+genotype,
   random=~row_group+column_group,residual=~idv(units),data=solo,
   na.action=asreml::na.method(y='fail',x='fail'),
   maxit=100,workspace='256mb',trace=FALSE)
 if(!isTRUE(solo_fit$converge))solo_fit<-update(solo_fit,maxit=100)
 stopifnot(isTRUE(solo_fit$converge),!anyDuplicated(solo$pot_id))
 co<-summary(solo_fit,coef=TRUE)$coef.fixed
 g<-levels(solo$genotype)
 ix<-match(paste0('genotype_',g),rownames(co))
 intercept_ix<-match('(Intercept)',rownames(co))
 ref_ix<-match(c(paste0('chapelle_',levels(solo$chapelle)[1]),
   paste0('resown_',levels(solo$resown)[1])),rownames(co))
 stopifnot(!anyNA(c(ix,intercept_ix,ref_ix)),
   all(co[ref_ix,'solution']==0))
 expected<-data.frame(genotype=g,
   solo_BLUE=co[intercept_ix,'solution']+co[ix,'solution'])
 baseline<-DGE[DGE$trait==t,c('genotype','prediction')]
 baseline$genotype<-as.character(baseline$genotype)
 matched<-merge(baseline,expected,by='genotype')
 stopifnot(nrow(matched)==length(g),!anyDuplicated(matched$genotype))
 test<-cor.test(matched$prediction,matched$solo_BLUE,method='pearson')
 solo_correlations[[t]]<-data.frame(trait=t,n_genotypes=nrow(matched),
   Pearson_R=unname(test$estimate),p_nominal=test$p.value)
 solo_comparisons[[t]]<-matched
 p<-ggplot(matched,aes(prediction,solo_BLUE))+
   geom_smooth(method='lm',formula=y~x,se=FALSE,
     colour='#B95442',linewidth=.7)+
   geom_point(size=2.5,colour='#277DA8')+
   geom_text(aes(label=genotype),vjust=-.8,size=3.5)+
   scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(.08,.15)))+
   labs(title=paste('Competition DGE versus solo BLUEs:',t),
     subtitle=sprintf('Pearson R = %.3f; nominal p = %s; n = %d',
       test$estimate,pfmt(test$p.value),nrow(matched)),
     x='Competition-model intercept + DGE',
     y='Design-adjusted solo intercept + genotype BLUE',
     caption='Chapelle 1, non-resown; random spatial effects zero.\nNominal p ignores uncertainty/covariance of estimated genotype values.')
 print(p)
}
solo_correlations<-dplyr::bind_rows(solo_correlations)
knitr::kable(solo_correlations,digits=4,row.names=FALSE)
```

`r if(nrow(solo_correlations))paste(sprintf('%s: Pearson R = %.3f, nominal p = %s (%d genotypes).',solo_correlations$trait,solo_correlations$Pearson_R,pfmt(solo_correlations$p_nominal),solo_correlations$n_genotypes),collapse=' ')else 'No trait selects M3, so no comparison is produced.'`

A positive correlation indicates that genotypes with larger DGE expectations
also tend to have greater solo performance. This is not a test of equality:
adding an intercept does not affect Pearson correlation, and high correlation
can coexist with different absolute yield levels. The p-value tests zero
correlation, not whether the correlation equals one.

Perfect correlation is not expected for several reasons:

- Solo performance and competition DGE are different quantities. The DGE
  baseline is estimated in two-plant pots with neighbour effects centred at
  zero; it is not an extrapolated absence-of-neighbour prediction.
- The two analyses use different observations and density/competition contexts.
  Each solo genotype has only three plants, making its adjusted mean noisy.
- Solo genotype effects are BLUEs without genetic shrinkage. Competition DGEs
  are BLUPs with shrinkage, informed by the joint DGE/IGE covariance and pair
  interaction model. Uniform shrinkage alone would preserve correlation; here
  information and adjustment can differ among genotypes.
- Design and variance parameters are estimated separately. Sampling error,
  unequal adjustments and genuine context-dependent genotype performance can
  all contribute. This plot cannot separate those explanations.

The correlation is descriptive: its nominal Pearson p-value ignores uncertainty
and covariance in the estimated genotype values. It does not by itself prove
that the underlying solo and competition genetic effects differ or agree.

## Numerical and residual diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
diagnostics<-bind_rows(lapply(traits,function(t){
 bind_rows(lapply(names(random_forms),function(m){
  f<-models[[t]][[m]];g<-genetic_block(f,m)
  data.frame(trait=t,model=m,converged=f$converge,loglik=f$loglik,
   DGE_IGE_correlation=g[['rho']])
 }))
}))
knitr::kable(diagnostics,digits=4,row.names=FALSE)
residual_data<-bind_rows(lapply(traits,function(t){
 m<-selection$selected[selection$trait==t];f<-models[[t]][[m]];d<-data_list[[t]]
 ok<-!is.na(d$response)
 data.frame(trait=t,residual=as.numeric(f$residuals)[ok],
 fitted=as.numeric(f$linear.predictors)[ok])
}))
```

```{r residual-checks, fig.path='ige_estimations/figures/', fig.height=9}
p1<-ggplot(residual_data,aes(sample=residual))+stat_qq(size=.6,alpha=.5)+
 stat_qq_line(colour='#B95442')+facet_wrap(~trait,scales='free',ncol=3)+
 labs(title='Selected-model residual Q-Q plots')
p2<-ggplot(residual_data,aes(fitted,residual))+geom_hline(yintercept=0,
 linetype=2,colour='#B95442')+geom_point(size=.6,alpha=.4)+
 facet_wrap(~trait,scales='free',ncol=3)+labs(title='Residuals versus fitted values')
patchwork::wrap_plots(p1,p2,ncol=1)
```

All `r nrow(diagnostics)` final models report convergence:
**`r all(diagnostics$converged)`**. Multiple starting correlations were tried
for M2/M3. Convergence does not validate the model assumptions. Q-Q plots of
raw conditional residuals are descriptive: shrinkage and pot correlation
mean they are not independent, identically distributed residual samples.
Tail departures, especially for PMG and counts, and changing residual spread
require investigation. Correlations near +/-1 make genetic components hard
to separate. Bootstrap LRTs and influence analyses would strengthen inference.

# Deliverables and reproducibility

This report holds the code, main tests, figures and interpretation. The
subfolders retain only figures and the genetic prediction/covariance tables.
Intermediate inputs, model RDS objects and the old without-pot-type comparison
are not needed to use the final predictions. Rerendering this report fits the
models anew from processed data and requires ASReml-R licensing, the listed
R packages, Pandoc and LaTeX.

Genetic effects are total genotype-level effects, not additive-only effects.
The exported normal-approximation errors describe within-model precision;
they do not justify assuming additive or rank-independent interactions in a
many-neighbour grid. Resowing is adjusted statistically; it is not a filter.
